problem: What is the domain in the $xy$-plane of the hyperbolic cylinder $(x+5)^{2}-{y}^{2}=1?$

feedback.problem: What is the domain in the $xy$-plane of the elliptic cylinder $\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{16}+\frac{(y+2)^{2}}{8}=1?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The full expression describing all points on our elliptic cylinder is

$$
\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{16}+\frac{(y+2)^{2}}{8}=1,\,z=k
$$

where $k\in R$ can vary arbitrarily. 

The domain of any cylinder in the $xy$-plane is its base curve. Hence, in this case, the domain is

$$
{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}:\text{ }\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{16}+\frac{(y+2)^{2}}{8}=1}
$$

which can be written as

$$
{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}:\text{ }\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{{4}^{2}}+\frac{(y+2)^{2}}{(2\sqrt{2})^{2}}=1}.
$$

This is an ellipse centered at $(1,-2)$ with semi-axes of lengths $4$ and $2\sqrt{2}.$

submitted_fields.submitted_value: An ellipse centered at $(1,-2)$ with semi-axes of lengths $4$ and $2\sqrt{2}.$
